controls.title: Security controls

inspector.title: Inspector
inspector.empty: Select an element on the map to see its details.
inspector.secret: {identity} ({kind, select, config {configuration file} other {cached in memory}}, readable as {level})
outcome.idle: Pick a scenario and run the attack.

outcome.summary: {steps, plural, one {# step} other {# steps}} · {nodes, plural, =0 {no element compromised} one {# element compromised} other {# elements compromised}} · {blocked, plural, =0 {no attempt blocked} one {# attempt blocked} other {# attempts blocked}}
timeline.empty: Run the attack to see its steps here.

why.noCouldBlock: No control of this lab stops this step.
compare.empty: Run the attack to compare with the same lab without any control.
compare.noneEnabled: No control is enabled yet. Switch one on in the Security controls panel, then run again.
text.noStory: The attack has not been run yet.
text.col.name: Name
technique.exploit-public-service.success: Exploits the service on port {port} of {node} from the Internet: code now runs there as {level}.
technique.exploit-public-service.blocked: Tries to exploit the service on port {port} of {node} from the Internet: blocked.
technique.exploit-remote-service.success: From {from}, exploits the service on port {port} of {node}: code now runs there as {level}.
technique.exploit-remote-service.blocked: From {from}, tries to exploit the service on port {port} of {node}: blocked.
technique.privilege-escalation.success: Becomes administrator on {node} through a flaw of its operating system.
technique.privilege-escalation.blocked: Tries to become administrator on {node}: blocked.
technique.credentials-in-files.success: Finds the credentials of {identity} in a configuration file on {node}.
technique.credentials-in-files.blocked: Looks for credentials in the configuration of {node}: none left.
technique.credential-dumping.success: Extracts the credentials of {identity} cached in the memory of {node}.
technique.credential-dumping.blocked: Tries to extract cached credentials on {node}: blocked.
technique.remote-login.success: From {from}, logs in to {node} on port {port} as {identity}: {level} access.
technique.remote-login.blocked: From {from}, tries to log in to {node} on port {port} as {identity}: blocked.
technique.database-access.success: From {from}, connects to the database of {node} as {identity} and reads {asset}.
technique.database-access.blocked: From {from}, tries to connect to the database of {node} as {identity}: blocked.
evidence.flow: {from} is allowed to open connections to {to} on port {port} (declared flow).
evidence.sameZone: {from} and {to} are in the same zone ({zone}), with no filtering between them.
evidence.flatNetwork: Nothing filters traffic from {fromZone} to {toZone}: {from} reaches {to} on port {port} although no such flow is needed (flat network).
evidence.weakness: The service on port {port} of {node} has a {weakness}.
evidence.unpatchedOs: The operating system of {node} is out of date.
evidence.foothold: The attacker already runs code on {node} as {level}.
evidence.privilege: {identity} is allowed to log in to {node} as {level}.
evidence.mfaNotApplicable: MFA would not help here: {identity} logs in to a {kind} service, which never asks for a second factor.
block.segmentation: Segmentation between {fromZone} and {toZone}: {from} cannot reach {to} on port {port}.
block.patch: {node} is up to date: the {weakness} is fixed.
block.vault: {node} no longer stores the credentials of {identity}.
block.mfa: {identity} needs a second factor to log in to {node}; the stolen secret alone is not enough.
